subject.title: fix(cron): support current and session: targets in initial delivery resolution

question: Should omitted delivery for direct `CronService.add` and declarative cron creation treat `current` and `session:<id>` as the same announce-default class as `isolated`, and where should that policy be canonically owned?
rationale: The branch changes persisted delivery defaults for callers that bypass normalization, while the surrounding cron code has related but not identical session-target responsibilities; tests and an older normalized CLI transcript cannot select the durable product boundary.

options.title: Centralize the shared policy before merge
options.body: Confirm the intended target set, then expose one canonical delivery-default predicate or creation boundary that normalization and direct-service callers both use.

options.title: Keep direct service isolated-only
options.body: Retain current direct-service behavior and close this PR if direct callers should require explicit delivery for persistent session targets.

options.title: Adopt the expanded default with explicit upgrade proof
options.body: Approve the new persisted default only after documenting why direct persistent-session callers should receive announce delivery and proving exact-head direct and declarative behavior.

recommendation.title: Centralize the shared policy before merge
recommendation.body: Confirm the intended target set, then expose one canonical delivery-default predicate or creation boundary that normalization and direct-service callers both use.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged persistent-session target work is the strongest available evidence of ownership for the contract this PR extends.
